title: Quit Corporate Job to Become Full-Time Indie Game Developer
planText: I am quitting my $130k software engineer job next month to develop a retro pixel-art RPG full-time. I have $25k in savings (about 5 months of living expenses). I have built game prototypes before but never shipped a commercial title. I plan to finish the game in 6 months, launch on Steam, and sustain myself from game sales.

pessimist.headline: Uncapped scope and zero marketing infrastructure will stall the game before release.

points.claim: Indie RPGs routinely suffer 2-3x timeline overruns from feature creep and engine bugs.
points.suggestedFix: Lock the feature scope to a 90-minute vertical slice with strict milestone freeze dates.

points.claim: First-time commercial Steam developers face zero algorithmic visibility without 7,000+ wishlists.
points.suggestedFix: Launch a Steam teaser page and publish bi-weekly development logs before committing full-time.

points.claim: Single point of failure on unvalidated gameplay mechanics can stall production after 4 months.
points.suggestedFix: Run a closed external playtest with 25 players using an itch.io build by month 2.

pessimist.verdict: Operational bottlenecks and lack of external playtesting threaten the delivery schedule.

accountant.headline: Mini-model shows liquidity exhaustion at month 5 before the game generates its first dollar.

points.claim: Model: $25k savings against $5k/mo personal burn gives 5 months runway, leaving a 1-month deficit before month 6 launch.
points.suggestedFix: Lower monthly living burn to an assumption: $3,200-$3,500/mo or preserve 8 months of expenses.

points.claim: Unit economics: at an assumption: $14.99 retail price, Steam 30% cut and taxes leave an assumption: $7.50-$8.50 net per copy.
points.suggestedFix: Model break-even unit volume at an assumption: 3,500-4,200 sales and test pricing on Steam forums.

points.claim: Overhead costs: Steam App Fee ($100), sound assets, and tooling require an assumption: $1,200-$2,000 unbudgeted capital.
points.suggestedFix: Allocate a dedicated $2,000 contingency line item specifically for commercial launch fees.

accountant.verdict: Net unit realization requires at least 3,800 units sold to replace basic monthly living burn.

skepticalParent.headline: You are trading hard-won stability for an isolated gamble without an agreed safety net.

points.claim: Walking away from employer health coverage and an established engineering team leaves you with zero safety net.
points.suggestedFix: Negotiate an unpaid leave of absence or part-time consulting contract with your current manager.

points.claim: You haven't communicated a clear fallback timeline to your loved ones if the game launch is delayed.
points.suggestedFix: If you have a partner or dependents, agree with them on a non-negotiable date to seek employment if targets are missed.

points.claim: Isolating yourself at home for six straight months strains your relationship with the people around you.
points.suggestedFix: Establish daily work-from-home boundaries and schedule weekly dinners outside the apartment.

skepticalParent.verdict: Pursue your passion, but build an honest safety perimeter with your loved ones first.

futureYou.headline: Looking back from five years out, each path carries an unavoidable form of regret.

points.claim: If I leave now, I think I'd regret the exhausting mental strain of building alone in isolation without external momentum.
points.suggestedFix: Commit to working from a public library or co-working space two days a week starting tomorrow.

points.claim: If I stay at the corporate desk, I think I'd regret watching other indie creators launch while I kept wondering what might have happened.
points.suggestedFix: Set aside two uninterrupted evenings this week to complete and playtest your core gameplay loop.

futureYou.verdict: Whichever path I pick, I think I will mourn the other; the real question is which flavor of regret I can carry.

optimist.headline: Strong technical competency and a dedicated niche audience provide genuine commercial leverage.

points.claim: Your proven professional software engineering background gives you high technical velocity and clean system architecture.
points.suggestedFix: Use proven open-source frameworks to prototype core gameplay loops within the first 3 weeks.

points.claim: Retro pixel-art RPGs possess highly passionate, viral sub-communities on Reddit and Discord eager to support indie creators.
points.suggestedFix: Post weekly pixel-art animation clips on social media to build organic advocates early.

points.claim: This advantage disappears entirely if the core narrative hook and combat feel are dull or derivative.
points.suggestedFix: Release a playable 10-minute battle demo on itch.io to validate core fun before building full content.

optimist.verdict: Your engineering foundation is an authentic differentiator if validated with early community feedback.

judge.rationale: Initial plan scored 23 due to a 5-month cash cliff against a 6-month dev cycle, unproven Steam discoverability, and solo burnout risk. The hardened plan raises survival to 52 by retaining part-time consulting income and requiring an early vertical slice milestone, accounting for realistic execution drag.
topRisks: Cash runway depletion at month 5 prior to commercial release
Steam discovery failure caused by launching without pre-built wishlist velocity
Isolation-induced development fatigue stalling milestone completion
judge.hardenedPlan: Phase 1 (Months 1-2, Employed): Build a 15-minute playable demo on itch.io; set up Steam page aiming for 3,000 wishlists; save an additional $6k. Phase 2 (Months 3-6, Hybrid): Transition to 15 hrs/week consulting (assumption: $3k/mo) while dedicating 30 hrs/week to game development. Phase 3 (Months 7-8): Finalize polish, participate in Steam Next Fest, and launch.

actionItems.task: Publish playable 15-minute prototype to itch.io for external feedback
Create Steam store page and submit capsule artwork
Negotiate 15-hour weekly contracting arrangement with current employer or network

keyTensions.summary: Pessimist and Skeptical Parent urged staying employed while Optimist pushed for speed; resolved by building demo while employed then transitioning to hybrid consulting.
Future You warned against burnout from pure solo isolation; resolved by enforcing weekly developer meetups and part-time client hours.

unresolvedQuestions: Will your current employer permit part-time contracting or a formal sabbatical?
What is your target retail price point relative to competing pixel-art indie RPGs?
